title: Development charge cut tied to provincial grant
subtitle: Also: 2027 fees and parking rates, budget timeline, parking penalties, fire routes, asset management, museum review.
overview: Council agreed in principle to cut residential development charges by 30% for three years, retroactive to March 30, 2026, as the condition of applying to the Ontario and Canada Development Charge Reduction Program {{vote:m13}}. The cut takes effect only if the City is approved for grant funding. Staff will apply for two water and sewer projects, with senior governments covering up to 90% of eligible costs and the City paying the rest from utility reserves.

Council also approved 2027 fees and charges across City departments. These include a 4% increase in monthly parking permits, no change to hourly parking rates, and a Parking Utilization Study {{vote:m10}}. Updated parking penalties and a Fire Route By-law amendment were approved as well.

Council endorsed the 2027 budget timeline, with the staff-tabled budget released December 14, 2026 and considered after February 1, 2027. It also approved policy revisions {{vote:m12}}. The projected 2026 tax base surplus is $293,000 {{vote:m1}}. Council received the asset management review and the Museum's 2025 review. A notice of motion on provincial water legislation was tabled for June 22.

decisions.detail: Council approved a 30% in-principle cut to residential development charges for three years and directed staff to apply for grant funding for the Conservation Drive pumping station and the Erbsville Road watermain, subject to approval of the grant {{vote:m13}}.
Council approved a 4% monthly permit increase and no hourly rate increase for 2027, and directed staff to include a Parking Utilization Study in the 2027 capital budget.
Council endorsed the 2027 budget and 2027-2030 Strategic Plan timelines and approved revisions to the capital budget and development charge interest policies, plus a new arts reserve fund policy.
Council approved the 2027 Community Services fees and charges by-law updates.
Council approved updated parking administrative penalties and fees and directed staff to bring forward the amending by-law.
Council approved amendments clarifying enforcement authority for fire routes in parks and on city lands.
Council acknowledged projected 2026 surpluses of $293,000 in the net tax base and $727,000 in the net Enterprise, and asked for a fall follow-up report.
Council approved the 2026 Asset Management Annual Review.

debate: On development charges, staff said the cut is in principle only and depends on securing grant funding. They said grant funding of about 90% compares well with the earlier core-area exemption, which the City funded entirely itself. Staff also said it is uncertain whether lower charges will produce more housing.

Two councillors opposed the development charge reduction. They said there is limited evidence it will increase housing or improve affordability. They also said it asks cities to subsidize developers while infrastructure needs go unmet, and that Council lacked detail on how the program would be run.

Supporters said applying shows commitment to housing, and that the grant is expected to exceed the revenue forgone. They pointed to exit options if funding falls short or the transfer agreement terms are a concern. Several still criticized the program's design and the compressed timeline.

On community services fees, councillors asked about affordability. Staff said part of the added revenue goes to the fee assistance and facility rental discount programs, and that cost pressures such as labour and chemicals are rising faster than general inflation. Councillors also asked staff to look at how not-for-profit groups are treated.

On parking, one councillor said three hours of Uptown parking costs less than a single transit trip. Staff said the planned utilization study and a later strategy would address this. Staff also said the new permit system has been delayed and will be re-tendered, possibly alongside licence plate recognition.
